name: AuxPair.exists_atPlace_eq
summary: It suffices to treat families with one nontrivial coordinate; for g_i at the place w_i take atSplit(w_i, g_i), which is supported on w_i and its conjugate and is 1 at the other places of O.

steps.claim: The image of the subgroup is a subgroup of the product, so it suffices to show that each family that is g_i at one index i and 1 at the others lies in it.
steps.lean:
atPlace (O.placeAt i)) := Subgroup.pi_mem_of_mulSingle_mem g fun i ↦
  ⟨atSplit (O.apart.2 i i) (g i), by simp; grind [atPlace_atSplit_of_ne],
  Function.eq_update_iff.2 (by simp_all [atPlace_atSplit_of_ne, O.apart.1.ne, O.apart.2])⟩

steps.claim: Take atSplit(w_i, g_i): w_i is split because no place of O is conjugate to a place of O.
It is supported on the places of O and their conjugates (its components off w_i and conj(w_i) are 1).
Its component at w_i is g_i and at every other place w_j of O it is 1, since the places of O are distinct and none is the conjugate of another.
